Scenario:
 
Draft a civil suit for partition along with a prayer for temporary injunction. Facts: Rupa is an adopted daughter of the deceased owner. She has no siblings. Her father died 5 years ago, leaving behind two flats in Pune. The only legal heirs are Rupa and her mother. Her name is not yet on the property documents. Her mother is attempting to dispossess her and has expressed intent to transfer the properties to her cousin. The suit should include legal provisions for partition of the properties, declaration of her share, and a temporary injunction restraining the mother or any third party from selling, transferring, or creating third-party rights in the properties until disposal of the suit.
 
Draft a civil suit for damages arising from medical negligence, incorporating detailed legal reasoning and relevant case laws. Scenario: My client, Mrs. Anjali Deshmukh, aged 42, and a resident of Pune, underwent gallbladder surgery at XYZ Multispecialty Hospital on 12th March 2024. During the procedure, the attending surgeon, Dr. Rakesh Nair, negligently caused damage to her bile duct. Following the surgery, she experienced severe abdominal pain and had to be admitted to another hospital for corrective surgery. As a result, she incurred additional medical expenses amounting to ₹3.5 lakhs and endured significant physical pain and mental agony. Despite repeated follow-ups, both the hospital and the doctor have refused to acknowledge their negligence or offer any compensation. Mrs. Deshmukh now seeks damages of ₹25 lakhs, covering medical expenses, mental harassment, pain and suffering, and anticipated costs of future treatment.

## Cause Title

IN THE COURT OF THE CIVIL JUDGE SENIOR DIVISION, PUNE

CIVIL SUIT NO. ______ OF 2024

Rupa [Father's Surname]
Daughter of Late [Father's Name],
Age: [Age],
Occupation: [Occupation],
Residing at: [Rupa's Current Address], Pune.

.....Plaintiff

**vs**

[Mother's Name]
Wife of Late [Father's Name],
Age: [Age],
Occupation: [Occupation],
Residing at: [Address of one of the flats], Pune.

.....Defendant

## Suit for Partition and Temporary Injunction

SUIT FOR PARTITION, DECLARATION, AND PERMANENT AND TEMPORARY INJUNCTION

The Plaintiff respectfully states as under:

1. That the Plaintiff files the present suit for partition of the suit properties, for a declaration that she is
entitled to a one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties, and for a permanent and temporary injunction restraining the
Defendant, her agents, or any person acting on her behalf from alienating, transferring, selling, or creating any
third-party rights in the suit properties. The suit is filed under the provisions of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the
Specific Relief Act, 1963, and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

## Facts of the Case

2. That the Plaintiff, Rupa, is the legally adopted daughter of the late [Father's Name] and the Defendant, [Mother's Name]. The Plaintiff has no biological or adopted siblings.

3. That the Plaintiff's adoptive father, the late [Father's Name], passed away intestate approximately five years ago. At the time of his demise, he was the absolute owner and was seized and possessed of two residential flats situated in Pune, the details of which are more particularly described in the Schedule of Properties annexed hereto and hereinafter referred to as the "suit properties".

4. That upon the death of the Plaintiff's father, the Plaintiff and the Defendant, being his daughter and widow respectively, are the only surviving Class I legal heirs as per the provisions of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

5. That by virtue of the laws of intestate succession, the Plaintiff and the Defendant are each entitled to an equal, undivided one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties and are in joint possession of the same.

6. That despite the Plaintiff's clear and indefeasible right, her name has not yet been mutated or entered into the official records pertaining to the suit properties. The Plaintiff has made several requests to the Defendant to cooperate in completing the necessary legal formalities and to effect an amicable partition of the suit properties by metes and bounds.

7. That the cause of action for the present suit arose recently when the Defendant began acting in a manner detrimental to the Plaintiff's interest. The Defendant has threatened to dispossess the Plaintiff from the residential property and has explicitly stated her intention to illegally alienate and transfer the suit properties to her cousin, thereby depriving the Plaintiff of her rightful share. This has created an immediate and urgent need for the intervention of this Hon'ble Court.

## Legal Provisions

8. That the present suit is maintainable under law. The Plaintiff, as an adopted daughter, is conferred with the same rights and status as a natural-born daughter under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956.

9. That under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the property of a Hindu male dying intestate devolves upon the heirs specified in Class I of the Schedule. The Plaintiff (daughter) and the Defendant (widow) are both Class I heirs and are entitled to succeed to the property of the deceased simultaneously and to the exclusion of all other heirs.

10. That the Plaintiff is entitled to seek a declaration of her one-half (1/2) share and a decree for partition and separate possession of the suit properties.

11. That in light of the Defendant's attempts to alienate the suit properties and create third-party rights, it is just and necessary to grant a temporary injunction under Order XXXIX, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, restraining the Defendant from doing so during the pendency of this suit, to prevent irreparable loss and injury to the Plaintiff.

12. That the reliefs of declaration and permanent injunction are sought under the relevant provisions of the Specific Relief Act, 1963.

## Plaintiff's Entitlement and Share

13. That the Plaintiff submits that as the legally adopted daughter of the deceased, Late [Father's Name], she is entitled to all the rights and privileges of a natural-born daughter. Upon the intestate demise of her father, his self-acquired properties, being the suit properties, devolved upon his Class I legal heirs as per the rules of succession laid down in the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

14. That according to Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the property of a Hindu male dying intestate devolves upon the heirs specified in Class I of the Schedule to the said Act. The Plaintiff, being the daughter, and the Defendant, being the widow, are the only two surviving Class I heirs of the deceased.

15. That as per the rules of distribution of property among Class I heirs, the Plaintiff and the Defendant are each entitled to an equal, undivided one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties. The Plaintiff's right, title, and interest in the suit properties are absolute and indefeasible, having vested in her immediately upon the death of her father.

## Grounds for Temporary Injunction

16. That the Plaintiff has a strong prima facie case in her favour. Her status as a Class I legal heir and her consequent entitlement to a one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties is established by law. The suit properties are joint family properties in which the Plaintiff has a vested, undivided interest.

17. That the balance of convenience is overwhelmingly in favour of the Plaintiff. Granting an injunction would merely
require the Defendant to maintain the status quo of the properties, causing her no prejudice. Conversely, refusing the
injunction would allow the Defendant to act upon her threats to alienate the properties. This would create irreversible
third-party rights, leading to a multiplicity of legal proceedings and rendering the present suit for partition
infructuous. The Plaintiff would be forced into protracted litigation against bona fide purchasers, causing immense
hardship.

18. That the Plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss and injury if the temporary injunction is not granted. The Defendant
has explicitly threatened to sell and transfer the suit properties to her cousin with the mala fide intention of
defeating the Plaintiff's legitimate claim. If the Defendant succeeds, the Plaintiff will be wrongfully deprived of her
rightful inheritance and may be dispossessed from her residence. Such a loss of immovable property cannot be adequately
compensated in monetary terms. The very subject matter of the suit would be lost, causing grave injustice to the
Plaintiff. Therefore, it is imperative to restrain the Defendant by an order of temporary injunction under Order XXXIX,
Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

## Jurisdiction and Valuation

19. That the suit properties are situated in Pune, which is within the territorial jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court. Therefore, this Hon'ble Court has the jurisdiction to try, entertain, and dispose of the present suit.

20. That for the purpose of court fees and jurisdiction, the suit is valued as follows:
a. For the relief of partition and separate possession of the Plaintiff's one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties, the suit is valued at Rs. [Value of Plaintiff's 1/2 Share], and the requisite court fee as prescribed under the Maharashtra Court Fees Act, 1959, has been paid thereon.
b. For the reliefs of declaration and permanent injunction, which are consequential to the main relief of partition, a fixed court fee has been paid as per the said Act.

21. That the total valuation of the suit for the purposes of jurisdiction is Rs. [Value of Plaintiff's 1/2 Share], and the appropriate court fee has been affixed to this plaint.

## Prayer

It is, therefore, most humbly and respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to:

a. Pass a preliminary decree for partition, declaring that the Plaintiff is the owner of and is entitled to a one-half (1/2) undivided share in the suit properties, more particularly described in the Schedule of Properties annexed hereto.

b. Pass a final decree for partition of the suit properties by metes and bounds and put the Plaintiff in separate, vacant, and peaceful possession of her one-half (1/2) share.

c. Grant a temporary injunction under Order XXXIX, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, restraining the Defendant, her agents, servants, or any person claiming through her, from selling, alienating, transferring, mortgaging, or creating any third-party rights, title, or interest in the suit properties during the pendency of this suit.

d. Pass a decree for permanent injunction restraining the Defendant and anyone acting on her behalf from interfering with the Plaintiff's right, title, interest, and possession in respect of her share in the suit properties.

e. Award the costs of this suit to the Plaintiff from the Defendant.

f. Grant any other and further reliefs as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.

## Verification

I, Rupa [Father's Surname], the Plaintiff abovenamed, do hereby solemnly state and verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to 21 of the foregoing plaint are true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information, and belief, and that nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at Pune on this ___ day of __________, 2024.

Plaintiff
(Rupa [Father's Surname])

## Cause Title

## Suit for Partition and Temporary Injunction

SUIT FOR PARTITION, DECLARATION, AND PERMANENT AND TEMPORARY INJUNCTION

The Plaintiff respectfully states as under:

1. That the Plaintiff files the present suit for partition of the suit properties, for a declaration that she is
entitled to a one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties, and for a permanent and temporary injunction restraining the
Defendant, her agents, or any person acting on her behalf from alienating, transferring, selling, or creating any
third-party rights in the suit properties. The suit is filed under the provisions of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the
Specific Relief Act, 1963, and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

## Facts of the Case

2. That the Plaintiff, Rupa, is the legally adopted daughter of the late [Father's Name] and the Defendant, [Mother's Name]. The Plaintiff has no biological or adopted siblings.

3. That the Plaintiff's adoptive father, the late [Father's Name], passed away intestate approximately five years ago. At the time of his demise, he was the absolute owner and was seized and possessed of two residential flats situated in Pune, the details of which are more particularly described in the Schedule of Properties annexed hereto and hereinafter referred to as the "suit properties".

4. That upon the death of the Plaintiff's father, the Plaintiff and the Defendant, being his daughter and widow respectively, are the only surviving Class I legal heirs as per the provisions of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

5. That by virtue of the laws of intestate succession, the Plaintiff and the Defendant are each entitled to an equal, undivided one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties and are in joint possession of the same.

6. That despite the Plaintiff's clear and indefeasible right, her name has not yet been mutated or entered into the official records pertaining to the suit properties. The Plaintiff has made several requests to the Defendant to cooperate in completing the necessary legal formalities and to effect an amicable partition of the suit properties by metes and bounds.

7. That the cause of action for the present suit arose recently when the Defendant began acting in a manner detrimental to the Plaintiff's interest. The Defendant has threatened to dispossess the Plaintiff from the residential property and has explicitly stated her intention to illegally alienate and transfer the suit properties to her cousin, thereby depriving the Plaintiff of her rightful share. This has created an immediate and urgent need for the intervention of this Hon'ble Court.

## Legal Provisions

8. That the present suit is maintainable under law. The Plaintiff, as an adopted daughter, is conferred with the same rights and status as a natural-born daughter under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956.

9. That under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the property of a Hindu male dying intestate devolves upon the heirs specified in Class I of the Schedule. The Plaintiff (daughter) and the Defendant (widow) are both Class I heirs and are entitled to succeed to the property of the deceased simultaneously and to the exclusion of all other heirs.

10. That the Plaintiff is entitled to seek a declaration of her one-half (1/2) share and a decree for partition and separate possession of the suit properties.

11. That in light of the Defendant's attempts to alienate the suit properties and create third-party rights, it is just and necessary to grant a temporary injunction under Order XXXIX, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, restraining the Defendant from doing so during the pendency of this suit, to prevent irreparable loss and injury to the Plaintiff.

12. That the reliefs of declaration and permanent injunction are sought under the relevant provisions of the Specific Relief Act, 1963.

## Plaintiff's Entitlement and Share

13. That the Plaintiff submits that as the legally adopted daughter of the deceased, Late [Father's Name], she is entitled to all the rights and privileges of a natural-born daughter. Upon the intestate demise of her father, his self-acquired properties, being the suit properties, devolved upon his Class I legal heirs as per the rules of succession laid down in the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

14. That according to Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the property of a Hindu male dying intestate devolves upon the heirs specified in Class I of the Schedule to the said Act. The Plaintiff, being the daughter, and the Defendant, being the widow, are the only two surviving Class I heirs of the deceased.

15. That as per the rules of distribution of property among Class I heirs, the Plaintiff and the Defendant are each entitled to an equal, undivided one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties. The Plaintiff's right, title, and interest in the suit properties are absolute and indefeasible, having vested in her immediately upon the death of her father.

## Grounds for Temporary Injunction

16. That the Plaintiff has a strong prima facie case in her favour. Her status as a Class I legal heir and her consequent entitlement to a one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties is established by law. The suit properties are joint family properties in which the Plaintiff has a vested, undivided interest.

17. That the balance of convenience is overwhelmingly in favour of the Plaintiff. Granting an injunction would merely
require the Defendant to maintain the status quo of the properties, causing her no prejudice. Conversely, refusing the
injunction would allow the Defendant to act upon her threats to alienate the properties. This would create irreversible
third-party rights, leading to a multiplicity of legal proceedings and rendering the present suit for partition
infructuous. The Plaintiff would be forced into protracted litigation against bona fide purchasers, causing immense
hardship.

18. That the Plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss and injury if the temporary injunction is not granted. The Defendant
has explicitly threatened to sell and transfer the suit properties to her cousin with the mala fide intention of
defeating the Plaintiff's legitimate claim. If the Defendant succeeds, the Plaintiff will be wrongfully deprived of her
rightful inheritance and may be dispossessed from her residence. Such a loss of immovable property cannot be adequately
compensated in monetary terms. The very subject matter of the suit would be lost, causing grave injustice to the
Plaintiff. Therefore, it is imperative to restrain the Defendant by an order of temporary injunction under Order XXXIX,
Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

## Jurisdiction and Valuation

19. That the suit properties are situated in Pune, which is within the territorial jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court. Therefore, this Hon'ble Court has the jurisdiction to try, entertain, and dispose of the present suit.

20. That for the purpose of court fees and jurisdiction, the suit is valued as follows:
a. For the relief of partition and separate possession of the Plaintiff's one-half (1/2) share in the suit properties, the suit is valued at Rs. [Value of Plaintiff's 1/2 Share], and the requisite court fee as prescribed under the Maharashtra Court Fees Act, 1959, has been paid thereon.
b. For the reliefs of declaration and permanent injunction, which are consequential to the main relief of partition, a fixed court fee has been paid as per the said Act.

21. That the total valuation of the suit for the purposes of jurisdiction is Rs. [Value of Plaintiff's 1/2 Share], and the appropriate court fee has been affixed to this plaint.

## Prayer

It is, therefore, most humbly and respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to:

a. Pass a preliminary decree for partition, declaring that the Plaintiff is the owner of and is entitled to a one-half (1/2) undivided share in the suit properties, more particularly described in the Schedule of Properties annexed hereto.

b. Pass a final decree for partition of the suit properties by metes and bounds and put the Plaintiff in separate, vacant, and peaceful possession of her one-half (1/2) share.

c. Grant a temporary injunction under Order XXXIX, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, restraining the Defendant, her agents, servants, or any person claiming through her, from selling, alienating, transferring, mortgaging, or creating any third-party rights, title, or interest in the suit properties during the pendency of this suit.

d. Pass a decree for permanent injunction restraining the Defendant and anyone acting on her behalf from interfering with the Plaintiff's right, title, interest, and possession in respect of her share in the suit properties.

e. Award the costs of this suit to the Plaintiff from the Defendant.

f. Grant any other and further reliefs as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.

## Verification

I, Rupa [Father's Surname], the Plaintiff abovenamed, do hereby solemnly state and verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to 21 of the foregoing plaint are true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information, and belief, and that nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at Pune on this ___ day of __________, 2024.

Plaintiff
(Rupa [Father's Surname])
